C1.rationale: Level 2 anchor met: core units run assessed group projects. The required capstone ENG 4002A/B (ENGI4022) is delivered as small-group work and its assessed deliverables (Report 55%, Report 20%, two Oral Defences) are the products of that group work, and the Level I core Introduction to Infrastructure is built on small-group analyses, designs and drawings. Not level 3: the only evidence of coordinating work across people AND tools/systems is a learning outcome in the Level III core Computer Analysis of Structures (group development and checking of a computer program plus analysis using commercial software), and that course's captured Assessment Tasks list is empty, so R2 bars a 3 - no core assessment documents the division of work between people and systems as itself assessed.
evidenceLines: Students work in small groups to create civil engineering analyses, designs and drawings. The group work will develop the key engineering attributes of working together in a team and professional communication skills.

C3.rationale: Level 1 anchor met: digital content in the core is tool operation and training - MATLAB and Excel programming, Matlab for statistical and numerical methods, and operating commercial structural-analysis software used in Australian industry - which is the operational level the anchor caps at 1. Not level 2: no core unit in the extract addresses AI or digital-tool capabilities together with their limitations or ethics. The single machine-learning treatment with critical evaluation of model types sits in Climate & Environmental Impact Modelling, a major/elective course, not the 66-unit core, and the anchor's level 1 explicitly covers AI appearing only in electives.

C4.rationale: Level 2 anchor met: the Level III core Hydrology and Flood Management assesses independent identification and application of the most appropriate flood-estimation technique to a catchment of interest through Design Project tasks worth 27% each - application to an unfamiliar problem, assessed. Held at 2 rather than 3 because the level-3 anchor's routes are not documented: the required Honours Research Project is scoped by supervisors, who provide the offerings, so the extract contradicts rather than supports 'self-scoped'; and no core assessment requires students to identify their own knowledge gaps together with a plan to close them. The self-directed-learning outcome in the Civil and Environmental Design Project cannot carry a 3 either, because that course's identity as the Level IV core CIVILENG 4050 Design Practice is not established by the extract.
evidenceLines: - Critically analyse, independently identify and apply the most appropriate flood estimation techniques to generate innovative solutions to complex engineering problems in flood estimation and management of a catchment of interest

C5.rationale: Level 3 anchor met on all three clauses. W1.rationale: Level 1 anchor met: professional communication and conduct are stated at program level (written and oral forms to lay and expert audiences; professional and ethical conduct) and in core course outcomes, and core assessment adds spoken communication to staff in the form of two assessed Oral Defence tasks in the capstone. Not level 2: no core assessment in the extract is documented as being in a recognised professional genre judged against criteria drawn from practice, or as reaching an audience beyond the teaching team. The Systems Engineering and Industry Practice outcomes about communicating to the broader community and to a generalist audience sit in a course whose captured Assessment Tasks list is empty, and R2 bars scoring an unassessed outcome; the professional-standard laboratory reporting outcome in Introduction to Geo-engineering is likewise unassessed in the extract.

W2.rationale: Level 3 anchor met on both clauses, scored on documented task features rather than any 'authentic' label (R4). Spine rather than a single instance: an assessed computer-based analysis project using commercial software used in Australian industry at Level II core Structural Mechanics (Assignment 35%), a Design Project worth 40% producing a reinforced-concrete design at Level III core Reinforced Concrete Design, Design Projects worth 27% each drawn from real world case studies at Level III core Hydrology and Flood Management, and the Level IV capstone Research Project assessed by report and oral defence - a capstone plus earlier scaffolding. Genuine constraint of practice: the profession's own standards of performance are the judging criteria (AS3600 for concrete, AS4100 for steel, the Australian Rainfall and Runoff national guidelines with industry-standard software), and the capstone problems are open ended.

W3.rationale: Held at level 1. The program does require 8 weeks of approved engineering work placement, which is stronger than the level-1 anchor's 'elective' or 'optional internship' framing, but the placement is carried by a 0-unit enrolment shell (ENG 3100 Engineering Internship UG) for which the extract captures no course page, and therefore documents none of the three features the level-2 anchor requires: practitioner supervision, assessment, and placement in a named workplace setting under those conditions. Level 1's 'unassessed' route is the closest documented state, and the scoring direction resolves the straddle downward. The in-practice route is not applicable: this is an undergraduate program with no cohort documented as already practising.

G1.rationale: PASS on the anchor's all-compulsory specialist core and accredited sequence, with progressive technical depth. The core is 66 units of named civil engineering courses compulsory at each of Levels I to IV, the program is accredited by Engineers Australia with graduates qualifying for professional membership, and depth is staged - Structural Mechanics precedes Reinforced Concrete Design and Structural Steel Design, and Civil Engineering Hydraulics precedes Advanced Civil Engineering Hydraulics. Content is disciplinary, not interchangeable.
evidenceLines: Core courses to the value of 66 units.
This program is accredited by Engineers Australia and graduates of the program qualify for professional membership of Engineers Australia.

The first and second years of the program develop mathematics and science skills, with fundamental engineering and design courses. Third and fourth years enable students to specialise and focuses on project based learning.

G2.rationale: PASS on the anchor's capstone-with-real-uncertainty route and its defended trade-off route. The required capstone assesses engineering solutions to complex, open ended problems through reports and two oral defences, and the Level III core Reinforced Concrete Design assesses design decisions informed by environmental impact through a 40% Design Project - a defended trade-off rather than recall. Recognising uncertainty and the limits of engineering approaches is an explicit outcome of the Level II core hydraulics course.

ambiguities: C1 straddled 1 and 2: the capstone's assessed items are reports and oral defences, and the extract does not state that collaboration itself is marked, only that the project is done in small groups. Resolved to 2 because the level-2 anchor names 'group projects' as the qualifying form and the group project's deliverables carry documented assessment weights; the level-1 anchor's 'no core unit assesses it' would be false here.

C4 straddled 2 and 3: a required two-semester honours research project preceded by a dedicated Level III research-methods course reads as structured progression toward independent learning, but the level-3 exemplar is a SELF-SCOPED capstone and the extract states supervisors provide the project offerings. Resolved DOWN to 2 under the lower-level rule.

W1 straddled 1 and 2: design reports and design documentation produced against AS3600, AS4100 and the Australian Rainfall and Runoff national guidelines are arguably recognised professional genres. Resolved DOWN to 1 because the extract documents neither the assessment criteria for those reports nor any audience beyond the teaching team, and because the fidelity of the design task is scored in W2 under the one-construct-one-home rule.

Course-page identity for the Level IV core: program rules list CIVILENG 4050 Design Practice as the sole Level IV core, and the extract carries two candidate pages - Civil and Environmental Design Project (ENGIX403, an industry-led capstone design with Concept Design and Design Project tasks worth 65%, an Interview worth 30% and a Portfolio worth 5%) and Design Practice (ENGM2015, a mechanical design introduction with an empty assessment list). Neither is confirmable as CIVILENG 4050, so ENGIX403 was not used to lift C2 (its Portfolio), C4 (its self-directed-learning outcome), W1 (its diverse-audience communication) or W2 above the level its other evidence already supports.

W3 straddled 1 and 2: the 8-week placement is compulsory, unlike the level-1 anchor's elective or optional framing, but level 2 additionally requires practitioner supervision and assessment, and the 0-unit enrolment shell documents neither. Resolved DOWN to 1.

C5: the capstone's project styles range across design-build-test, industry-focused and research-orientated work, so not every student's project is research-shaped. Scored 3 regardless because every listed style generates primary evidence (theoretical analyses, simulations and experiments) and the defence and staged Part A review apply to all of them.
notScoreable: ENG 3100 Engineering Internship UG - no course page was captured for the 0-unit placement shell, so its supervision arrangements, assessment (if any) and reflective requirements could not be scored; W3 was scored on the program-rules text alone.
CIVILENG 3006 Geotechnical Engineering (Level III core) - no matching course page appears in the extract, so its assessment contributed to no item.

Assessment tables are empty for a large share of the core: Introduction to Infrastructure, Engineering Mechanics - Statics, Introduction to Engineering, Programming (Matlab and Excel), Mathematics IA, Strength of Materials, Civil Engineering Hydraulics, Introduction to Geo-engineering, Transportation Engineering & Survey, Statistics & Numerical Methods II, Computer Analysis of Structures and Structural Dynamics, Advanced Civil Engineering Hydraulics, Systems Engineering and Industry Practice, and Research Methods and Project Management. Every level-2 and level-3 judgement above therefore rests only on the subset of core courses whose assessment weights were captured, and C1, C2 and W1 in particular could move up if those tables were captured.
